To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

bisantrene binds to DNA with a helix-unwinding angle of 15 degrees and causes an increase of 2.7A in DNA contour length per bound drug molecule, with a bimolecular rate of binding of 2 X 10(8) M-1 s- 1.

bisantrene binds DNA with a helix-unwinding angle of 13 degrees per bound molecule, with a bimolecular rate of association greater than 10(7)s-1 M-1, and that the dissociation kinetics are complex, involving at three distinguishable processes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the elucidation of the mode of binding of bis(2,6-dioxopiperazine)anthracene-9,10-dione (bisantrene) to covalently closed circular DNA, and to sonicated rod-like DNA fragments.
the elucidation of the mode and kinetics of DNA intercalation of a series of bisantrene analogs.
the mode and kinetics of binding of the anti-cancer drug, bisantrene, to DNA.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the binding of bisantren to DNA is a fast and tight process, with an affinity of 7- 8 X 10 M-1 and a helix unwind angle of about 14 degrees.
bisantrene binds to DNA by intercalation, but that the kinetics of binding and dissociation are complex.
bisantrene binds DNA with an apparent intercalative mechanism, and the rate-limiting step for dissociation is the release of the bound drug from the helix.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
bisantrene binds with a helix-unwinding angle of 13 degrees, a DNA lengthening of 3A, a dissociation constant of 7 X 10(8) M-1, and a bimolecular rate of binding of 1 X 107 M-1 s- 1.
bisantrene is a relatively fast-binding, moderately tight-binding intercalating agent, which binds with a relatively small helix unwinding.

bisantrene binds to DNA with high affinity and with an intercalative binding mode, but that it is relatively unstable in its bound state, with an average half-life of 0.3-0.5 s at ionic strength 100 mM and 20 degrees C for one drug molecule bound to a 20 base pair fragment of DNA.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the binding mechanism of bisantrene is not a simple one.
bisantrene is an effective DNA intercalator, and its association and dissociation with DNA are fast.
, although the DNA binding properties of bisantrene have been known for some time, the mechanism of its association with DNA is still poorly understood.
